Daily Brief

Germany's political landscape faces its most significant test in decades after the far-right AfD secured 43.8% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt, falling just three seats short of an outright majority [BBC Europe, RFI]. Chancellor Friedrich Merz acknowledged the result as 'seismic' while the AfD pushes for coalition talks, challenging the long-standing firewall against far-right governance [Le Monde, France 24]. Transatlantic trade tensions escalated as Canada's counter-tariffs on nearly C$28 billion worth of US goods took effect, with no resumption of negotiations in sight [BBC World]. The EU moved to strengthen ties with Greenland through a €200 million investment package, with Commission President von der Leyen explicitly pushing back against US territorial claims [RFI]. In the Middle East, the UK announced plans to ban trade with illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank, a move that drew sharp criticism from Israeli officials and risks friction with Washington [Al Jazeera, Financial Times]. Regional instability deepened as Houthi strikes injured dozens across southern Saudi Arabia while Russia resumed missile attacks on Kyiv after a three-day pause [Al Jazeera, Le Monde, Financial Times].

Top Stories
01 Geopolitics

AfD Wins Historic Victory in Saxony-Anhalt, Threatening Germany's Anti-Far-Right Firewall

  • The AfD won 43.8% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt's state election, securing 39 of 83 seats—three short of an outright majority
  • Chancellor Friedrich Merz's CDU received just 17.2%, roughly half its previous result, which Merz called 'the heaviest electoral defeat the CDU has suffered in decades'
  • AfD deputy leader Beatrix von Storch called on other parties to enter coalition talks, stating 'democracy demands' they work with the election winners
  • No far-right party has controlled a German state since World War Two; the AfD is classified as a 'right-wing extremist' organisation by Germany's domestic intelligence agency

02 Economics

Canada's Retaliatory Tariffs on $20 Billion in US Goods Take Effect as Trade Talks Stall

  • Counter-tariffs of up to 50% now apply to nearly C$28 billion ($20 billion) worth of American products including steel, furniture, and cotton textiles
  • Fresh fish and lobster were removed from the tariff list after pushback from Canada's seafood industry
  • Talks collapsed in late August with no movement toward resumption; US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said 'the ball is in Canada's court'
  • Prime Minister Mark Carney stated Canada seeks a 'durable' deal and remains ready to negotiate when the US is willing

03 Geopolitics

EU Unveils €200 Million Greenland Investment Package Amid Trump's Territorial Claims

  • European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the investment package during a two-day visit to Nuuk, coming on top of doubled direct EU aid to Greenland
  • Von der Leyen stated 'Greenland's future is for the people of Greenland and Denmark to decide, no one else,' directly addressing US pressure
  • The package aims to support concrete development projects and strengthen EU engagement in the Arctic region
  • Trump earlier insisted the US needed to control Greenland for national security reasons but ruled out annexation by force

04 Policy

UK to Ban Trade with Illegal Israeli Settlements in West Bank

  • Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband will present measures to Parliament banning trade with goods from illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank
  • The move responds to Israel's recent opening of bidding for 1,234 housing units in the controversial E1 settlement project
  • Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for expulsion of the British ambassador and accused the UK of being 'conquered by radical Islam'
  • UK officials clarified this is not intended as a boycott of all Israeli goods, with Israel remaining an important trading partner
